direct_facts: Alija Alic testified that he was Tactical Group II chief of staff.
He testified that Serb forces controlled Rogoj in July 1992.
He testified that Tactical Group II attacked Trnovo simultaneously with its effort against Rogoj Pass on 1992-07-31.
Separate testimony says the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina took over Trnovo on 1992-07-31.

source.case: Prosecutor v. Kunarac et al., IT-96-23-T & IT-96-23/1-T

limited_inferences: The cited evidence strongly places Tactical Group II on the Bosnian-government side but does not state its exact formal chain-of-command label.
The same-date statements do not prove Tactical Group II alone captured Trnovo.
1992-07-31 lies within the seven-day span beginning at the t16 label 1992-07-27, so chronology is compatible but identity with authored Operation Circle is unproven.
excluded_inferences: Donje Zesce or Tosici aggregate capture chain

direct_facts: The order came from Foca Tactical Group commander Colonel Marko Kovac.
The transcript translates its objective as breaking the siege of Gorazde.
The exhibit bore the stamp of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Autonomous District of Herzegovina.
The Mladic judgment places Foca Tactical Group in the VRS reporting structure and names Serbian-side formations ordered by Kovac.

sources.case: Prosecutor v. Kunarac et al., IT-96-23-T & IT-96-23/1-T
sources.short_quote: order to break the siege of Gorazde

clarifications.limited_inference: It is a Serbian-side offensive order.
clarifications.ambiguity: The cited English wording does not identify besieger, besieged force, intended beneficiary, or whether the order aimed to end a siege of the RBiH-held city.
clarifications.safe_description: Serbian-side Foca Tactical Group order whose translated objective was to break the siege of Gorazde.
clarifications.excluded_inference: ARBiH order of battle or authorship
